title: Simple Machines
intro: Levers, pulleys, planes and gears — the six machines hiding inside every jembe, mkokoteni, bicycle and posho mill.

lessons.title: What Machines Do for Us
lessons.focus: Machines change force size, direction or speed; input/output; open the unit by lifting a heavy stone three ways.
lessons.advanced: A machine can't multiply work: explain the force-distance trade as conservation of energy.

lessons.title: Mechanical Advantage and Velocity Ratio
lessons.focus: MA = load/effort; VR = effort distance/load distance; efficiency = MA/VR; measure both on a simple lever.
lessons.advanced: Lever gives VR 4 but measured MA 3.2: compute efficiency and name the loss.

lessons.title: Levers Class 1: Seesaws, Crowbars and Pliers
lessons.focus: Fulcrum between effort and load; seesaw balancing different weights by distance; crowbar pulling nails.
lessons.advanced: 40 kg child balances 70 kg adult on a 3 m seesaw: find each distance from the fulcrum.

lessons.title: Levers Class 2: Wheelbarrows and Bottle Openers
lessons.focus: Load between fulcrum and effort; wheelbarrow physics; bottle opener and nutcracker anatomy.
lessons.advanced: Wheelbarrow: load 400 N at 0.4 m from wheel, handles at 1.2 m: find the lifting effort.

lessons.title: Levers Class 3: The Mwiko and the Human Arm
lessons.focus: Effort between fulcrum and load; mwiko stirring, fishing rod, tweezers; trading force for speed and reach.
lessons.advanced: Why did evolution pick class-3 arms? Discuss speed/force trade with biceps-at-4 cm numbers.

lessons.title: Moments: The Turning Force
lessons.focus: Moment = F × d from pivot; balance a ruler with unequal bottle-top piles by sliding positions.
lessons.advanced: 5 tops at 20 cm balance 8 tops at what distance? Then generalize: write the balance rule.

lessons.title: Law of Moments Lab: Weighing Without a Scale
lessons.focus: Balance an unknown stone against known water volumes on a ruler; compute the stone's mass.
lessons.advanced: Known 300 g at 18 cm balances unknown at 12 cm: compute unknown mass; list error sources.

lessons.title: Centre of Gravity: The Balance Point
lessons.focus: Balance a jembe and a broom on a finger; CG of regular vs irregular shapes; plumb line method with string+nut.
lessons.advanced: Use the plumb-line intersection method on a cut-out of Kenya: describe where the CG lands and why.

lessons.title: Levers in the Human Body
lessons.focus: Neck (class 1), calf raise (class 2), biceps (class 3); posture and load; why lifting with bent back hurts.
lessons.advanced: Head mass 5 kg tilted 30° shifts its line of action: explain the extra neck moment and 'text neck' fatigue.

lessons.title: Carrying Loads: The Physics of Head Portering
lessons.focus: Head carrying aligns load over spine; tump lines on foreheads; kiondo straps; energy studies show head loads are efficient.
lessons.advanced: Compare carrying 20 kg on head vs one shoulder: draw force lines and predict muscle effort differences.

lessons.title: Build: A Graduated Weighing Beam I
lessons.focus: Make a steelyard-style beam: fixed pan, sliding stone weight, notches calibrated with water (100 g = 100 mL).
lessons.advanced: Explain the sliding-weight principle with moments; why are the notches evenly spaced?

lessons.title: Build: A Graduated Weighing Beam II — Test and Certify
lessons.focus: Weigh five known items, plot error, adjust notches; 'certify' the beam with a class stamp.
lessons.advanced: Beam reads 5% high at 1 kg but exact at 500 g: diagnose a systematic cause and fix it.

lessons.title: The Wheel and Axle
lessons.focus: Mkokoteni wheel, doorknob, screwdriver, steering: big wheel turns small axle with multiplied force.
lessons.advanced: Windlass drum 4 cm radius, handle 40 cm: compute VR; how does that map to force on the rope?

lessons.title: Build: The Well Windlass
lessons.focus: Spool + crank + string + small bucket; lift 'water' from a desk-well; measure effort vs direct lift.
lessons.advanced: Measure effort with and without the crank; compute MA and discuss friction at the axle.

lessons.title: The Inclined Plane I: Ramp vs Lift
lessons.focus: Roll debe up a plank instead of lifting; same work, less force, more distance; measure with spring balance.
lessons.advanced: Ramp 3 m long, 1 m rise, 100 N load: ideal effort vs measured 45 N — efficiency?

lessons.title: The Inclined Plane II: Switchbacks and Loading Planks
lessons.focus: Hill paths zigzag; loading mkokoteni with planks; wheelchair ramps; measure effort vs ramp angle on a model.
lessons.advanced: Plot effort vs sin(angle) from your data: confirm the proportionality and extract the load's weight.

lessons.title: The Wedge: Pangas, Axes and Jembe Tips
lessons.focus: Two inclined planes back to back; splitting firewood; why thin sharp wedges need less force; sharpening as physics.
lessons.advanced: A wedge 10 cm long, 2 cm thick driven by 200 N: ideal splitting force? (VR = length/thickness.)

lessons.title: The Screw: A Spiral Inclined Plane
lessons.focus: Unwrap a paper triangle from a bottle thread; car screw jack lifting a vehicle; G-clamp force; wood screws vs nails.
lessons.advanced: Jack pitch 3 mm, handle 30 cm: compute VR per turn and ideal load for 200 N effort.

lessons.title: Pulleys I: The Fixed Pulley
lessons.focus: Flagpole and well pulley change direction only; build fixed pulley from a spool/wire hanger; MA = 1, comfort = high.
lessons.advanced: If a fixed pulley gives no force advantage, why do wells still use them? Three physical reasons.

lessons.title: Pulleys II: The Movable Pulley Halves the Effort
lessons.focus: One fixed + one movable; count supporting strands = ideal MA; measure real effort vs prediction.
lessons.advanced: Two-strand system lifts 100 N with measured 60 N: ideal effort, efficiency, and where 10 N went.

lessons.title: Block and Tackle: The Jua Kali Engine Hoist
lessons.focus: Chain blocks lifting engines; rig a 4-strand system; the long pull for a big lift; safety under suspended loads.
lessons.advanced: 4-strand tackle, load 800 N, efficiency 70%: effort required and rope pulled for a 0.5 m lift.

lessons.title: Pulley Lab: Effort vs Strand Count
lessons.focus: Systematically measure effort for 1,2,3,4 strands; plot effort vs 1/strands; discuss friction's growing share.
lessons.advanced: Fit your data to effort = W/(n·η): estimate η per strand and explain the downward trend.

lessons.title: Gears: Trading Speed for Force
lessons.focus: Bicycle gears; big cog slow-strong, small cog fast-weak; count teeth, compute ratios; drawgear on posho mill teaser.
lessons.advanced: Front 44 teeth, rear 11 vs 28: compute wheel turns per pedal turn and the climbing advantage ratio.

lessons.title: Belt Drives: Posho Mills and Sewing Machines
lessons.focus: Belt connects pulleys; crossed vs open belt direction; slipping as a safety feature; tension adjustment.
lessons.advanced: Driver 10 cm, driven 30 cm: compute speed ratio and torque ratio for the posho mill.

lessons.title: The Bicycle: A Machine Made of Machines I
lessons.focus: Identify lever (pedals, brakes), wheel-axle, gears, chain drive, bearings, screws on a real boda bicycle.
lessons.advanced: Trace the force path from foot to road, naming every machine and its MA contribution.

lessons.title: The Bicycle II: Measuring Its Advantages
lessons.focus: Count gear teeth, measure pedal-arm and wheel radii, compute real ratios; brake lever MA; present findings.
lessons.advanced: Combine pedal lever (0.17 m), chainring/cog ratio and wheel radius into one force multiplication number.

lessons.title: The Treadle Sewing Machine: Foot to Needle
lessons.focus: Treadle (lever) → crank → flywheel (rotation smoothed) → belt → needle; energy storage in the flywheel.
lessons.advanced: Explain how the flywheel's stored energy carries the mechanism past the 'dead spots' of each stitch cycle.

lessons.title: Design Challenge: A Machine for Our Village I
lessons.focus: Teams choose a real task (lifting water, shelling maize, pressing tiles); sketch using ≥3 simple machines; peer review.
lessons.advanced: Estimate the combined MA and efficiency of your design from component values.

lessons.title: Design Challenge II: Build and Demonstrate
lessons.focus: Build the chosen machine from jua kali scrap and school materials; demonstrate lifting/moving a real load.
lessons.advanced: Measure actual MA with a spring balance; compare with design prediction and explain the gap.

lessons.title: Why Machines Waste Energy
lessons.focus: Friction in axles and ropes; efficiency measured across the unit's builds; lubrication and alignment as cures.
lessons.advanced: Rank the class builds by efficiency and propose one modification each that raises η by ≥10%.

lessons.title: Maintenance Matters: Oiling, Tightening, Aligning
lessons.focus: Boda service schedule as physics: chain lube, brake pads, bearing play; write a maintenance card for a class build.
lessons.advanced: Quantify: a dry chain wastes ~5% of pedal energy — how many extra food kJ per 10 km ride?

lessons.title: Unit Review: Machine Fair
lessons.focus: Every build on show with student explainers; visitors operate each; unit quiz.
lessons.advanced: Prepare a 2-minute explainer for one machine: include MA, VR, efficiency and one safety rule.
